turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: His apprehensions were his own, Sandip, and required no explanation to him. The persistence in probing motives felt tedious and unproductive; he suggested that Sandip direct energies elsewhere.
turns.speech: My apprehensions are my own, Sandip, and require no explanation to you. Your persistence in probing my motives is tedious and unproductive; I suggest you direct your energies elsewhere.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Must they always dissect every feeling, Sandip? It seemed a great deal of energy was expended on uncovering what may or may not be hidden, rather than simply…being.
turns.speech: Must we always dissect every feeling, Sandip? It seems a great deal of energy is expended on uncovering what may or may not be hidden, rather than simply…being.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, Bimala, he remarked, ever the peacemaker, attempting to diffuse the tempest with platitudes! But he turned to Nikhil, asking if he was truly so impervious to the winds of change. He insisted he merely observed – a student of history, as it were – and history, he declared, was replete with examples of those who dismissed whispers of discontent until it was far too late.
turns.speech: Ah, Bimala, ever the peacemaker, attempting to diffuse the tempest with platitudes! But tell me, Nikhil, are you truly so impervious to the winds of change? I merely observe, you see – a student of history, as it were – and history, my dear fellow, is replete with examples of those who dismissed whispers of discontent until it was far too late.

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: History, he said to Sandip, was a heavy cloak to wear. It served them, did it truly, to dwell so constantly on the past’s potential for upheaval, when the present demanded such…attention?
turns.speech: History…it is a heavy cloak to wear, Sandip. Does it truly serve us to dwell so constantly on the past's potential for upheaval, when the present demands such…attention?

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Indeed, Bimala, he observed, a heavy cloak it felt, and yet, was it not the weight of history that anchored them, prevented them from dissolving into the ephemeral whims of the present? He merely suggested, Nikhil, that ignoring the rustling beneath the surface—the murmurs of the *ulema*, for instance—was akin to Nero fiddling while Rome… well, he was certain Nikhil would grasp the analogy.
turns.speech: Indeed, Bimala, a heavy cloak, and yet, is it not the weight of history that anchors us, prevents us from dissolving into the ephemeral whims of the present? I merely suggest, Nikhil, that ignoring the rustling beneath the surface—the murmurs of the *ulema*, for instance—is akin to Nero fiddling while Rome… well, you grasp the analogy, I'm certain.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: The *ulema*'s pronouncements were matters of religious conviction, Sandip, and he was not qualified to assess their influence. He trusted his tenants possessed the discernment to navigate their own spiritual lives without needing his intervention, nor, he suspected, Sandip's prompting.
turns.speech: The *ulema*'s pronouncements are matters of religious conviction, Sandip, and I am not qualified to assess their influence. I trust my tenants possess the discernment to navigate their own spiritual lives without needing my intervention, nor, I suspect, your prompting.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Discernment, Sandip asked, Nikhil? It was a comforting word, easily dispensed. But he wondered, did one truly possess discernment when one’s ears were so carefully plugged against the voices that disagreed, against the realities that were…uncomfortable? It was a dangerous sort of blindness, he suggested.
turns.speech: Discernment, you say, Nikhil? A comforting word, easily dispensed. But I wonder, does one truly possess discernment when one’s ears are so carefully plugged against the voices that disagree, against the realities that are…uncomfortable? It’s a dangerous sort of blindness, wouldn’t you agree?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Blindness, Sandip, was a condition easily attributed to those one wished to discredit. He assured Sandip that he was not wilfully ignorant, merely occupied with the practical concerns of managing his estate and ensuring the well-being of those who depended on it. Idle speculation regarding the motives of religious leaders, he felt, did little to address those concerns.
turns.speech: Blindness, Sandip, is a condition easily attributed to those one wishes to discredit. I assure you, I am not wilfully ignorant, merely occupied with the practical concerns of managing my estate and ensuring the well-being of those who depend on it. Idle speculation regarding the motives of religious leaders does little to address those concerns.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Practical concerns, Nikhil? How very… domestic. He confessed that he found himself increasingly drawn to matters that extended beyond the immediate yield of the fields, beyond the comfortable certainty of one's holdings. One must, after all, consider the larger landscape, mustn't one?
turns.speech: Practical concerns, you say, Nikhil? How very… domestic. I confess, I find myself increasingly drawn to matters that extend beyond the immediate yield of the fields, beyond the comfortable certainty of one's holdings. One must, after all, consider the larger landscape, mustn't one?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: The ‘larger landscape,’ as Sandip called it, often obscured the details that demanded immediate attention. He felt responsible for the welfare of many, and could not afford to be distracted by abstract notions of some grand, unfolding drama. His focus remained where it must be: on the fields, the harvests, and the people who worked them.
turns.speech: The ‘larger landscape,’ as you call it, Sandip, often obscures the details that demand immediate attention. I am responsible for the welfare of many, and I cannot afford to be distracted by abstract notions of some grand, unfolding drama. My focus remains where it must be: on the fields, the harvests, and the people who work them.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Ah, responsibility, Sandip said to Nikhil. It was a noble burden, certainly, but one that he found could become rather stifling. He wondered if it occasionally felt as though one were merely a caretaker, preserving a garden that was already in decline, rather than a cultivator, nurturing something new and vibrant?
turns.speech: Ah, responsibility, Nikhil. A noble burden, certainly, but one that can, I find, become rather… stifling. Does it not occasionally feel as though one is merely a caretaker, preserving a garden that is already in decline, rather than a cultivator, nurturing something new and vibrant?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: Such metaphors, Sandip, were needlessly dramatic. He acknowledged the weight of his responsibilities, and he did not dismiss the need for adaptation; however, indulging in pessimistic comparisons served no practical purpose and did little to improve the ‘garden’ he suggested was in decline.
turns.speech: Such metaphors, Sandip, are needlessly dramatic. I acknowledge the weight of my responsibilities, and I do not dismiss the need for adaptation; however, indulging in pessimistic comparisons serves no practical purpose and does little to improve the ‘garden’ you suggest is in decline.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: A garden in decline, he asked Nikhil. How very perceptive of him, Nikhil. But he wanted to know if a gardener was truly admirable if he merely tended to weeds, meticulously pruning what little beauty remained, while ignoring the encroaching wilderness just beyond the fence? He trusted Nikhil understood the implications of such a… neglect.
turns.speech: A garden in decline, you say? How very perceptive of you, Nikhil. But tell me, is a gardener truly admirable if he merely tends to weeds, meticulously pruning what little beauty remains, while ignoring the encroaching wilderness just beyond the fence? I trust you understand the implications of such a… neglect.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: He told Sandip that he was not accustomed to interpreting riddles. If he had a concern regarding the security of his property or the well-being of those who depended on it, he would prefer he address it directly, rather than cloaking it in such elaborate imagery.
turns.speech: I am not accustomed to interpreting riddles, Sandip. If you have a concern regarding the security of my property or the well-being of those who depend on it, I would prefer you address it directly, rather than cloaking it in such elaborate imagery.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Directness, he remarked to Nikhil, a touch of amusement in his voice. How refreshing. But he wondered, did a man who insisted on clarity truly *want* to see what lies beneath the surface, or merely prefer the comfortable illusion of order? He suspected, in Nikhil’s case, it was the latter, and he turned to Bimala, adding, wouldn’t she agree?
turns.speech: Directness, you say? How refreshing, Nikhil. But tell me, does a man who insists on clarity truly *want* to see what lies beneath the surface, or merely prefers the comfortable illusion of order? I suspect, in your case, it’s the latter, wouldn’t you agree, Bimala?

turns.speaker: Bimala
turns.text: Perhaps, Sandip, he thought she overestimated his understanding of such things. She found herself more concerned with the fragrance of the flowers within the garden than with the imagined dangers lurking beyond the fence, though she admitted shadows could be quite intriguing.
turns.speech: Perhaps, Sandip, you overestimate my understanding of such things. I find myself more concerned with the fragrance of the flowers within the garden than with the imagined dangers lurking beyond the fence, though I admit, shadows can be quite intriguing.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: It was intriguing, Bimala, he observed, that she prioritized scent over shadow. It reminded him of Baudelaire, he knew—the exquisite allure of decay. He then turned to Nikhil, asking if he was *certain* his garden was so well-tended that he could afford to ignore the whispers carried on the wind, the fervent pronouncements echoing from the mosques. Some gardens, he explained, attracted more than just bees.
turns.speech: Intriguing, Bimala, your prioritization of scent over shadow. It reminds me of Baudelaire, you know—the exquisite allure of decay. But tell me, Nikhil, are you *certain* your garden is so well-tended that you can afford to ignore the whispers carried on the wind, the fervent pronouncements echoing from the mosques? Some gardens, you see, attract more than just bees.

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: He found Sandip’s literary allusions tiresome. Nikhil felt responsible for the well-being of his household and tenants; speculation about the motives of religious leaders did little to aid that responsibility. He suggested they speak plainly, and if there was a genuine concern, it should be stated.
turns.speech: I find your literary allusions tiresome, Sandip. I am responsible for the well-being of my household and tenants; speculation about the motives of religious leaders does little to aid that responsibility. Let us speak plainly, if you have a genuine concern, state it.

turns.speaker: Sandip
turns.text: Plainly? How very… pedestrian, Nikhil. He observed that some men, consumed by their immediate harvests, failed to notice the storm clouds gathering on the horizon – clouds that, he assured them, were not conjured from mere whispers. It was a simple matter of perspective, wouldn't she agree, Bimala?
turns.speech: Plainly? How very… pedestrian, Nikhil. I merely observe that some men, consumed by their immediate harvests, fail to notice the storm clouds gathering on the horizon – clouds that, I assure you, are not conjured from mere whispers. It is a simple matter of perspective, wouldn't you agree, Bimala?

turns.speaker: Nikhil
turns.text: His concern lay with the practical realities of this household, not the interpretation of poetic metaphors. If he possessed information regarding a genuine threat to his family or tenants, he requested that it be presented directly; otherwise, he found the conversation unproductive.
turns.speech: My concern lies with the practical realities of this household, not the interpretation of poetic metaphors. If you possess information regarding a genuine threat to my family or tenants, I request you present it directly; otherwise, I find this conversation unproductive.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip inquired of Bimala as to where she intended to flee, addressing her as Queen.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip remarked to Nikhil that he questioned why Browning was not among his books, recalling a conversation with Bimala about a college contest involving Browning's translation, and asking if Nikhil remembered it.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip explained to Nikhil that he had managed to translate Browning into Bengali, though the result was far from a lasting joy for Bengal, and that he once believed himself on the verge of becoming a poet, but Providence had intervened. He then recalled old Dakshina, suggesting that had he not become a Salt Inspector, he would have been a poet.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip informed Bimala that it was pointless for her to search the bookshelves, as Nikhil had ceased reading poetry since his marriage, and that he suspected a return of his poetic inspiration.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip stated that Nikhil had come to give him a warning.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip inquired of Nikhil whether the warning concerned his poetic inspiration.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil told Sandip that Mahomedan preachers had been stirring up the local Mussulmans, who were agitated and might attack him at any moment.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip asked Nikhil if he had come to advise flight.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil clarified to Sandip that he had come to provide information, not to offer advice.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip commented to Nikhil that a warning would have been necessary for the preachers, not for him, had the estates been his, and suggested that Nikhil's weakness was also undermining neighboring zamindars.

opening.speaker: Nikhil
opening.text: Nikhil pointed out to Sandip that he had not offered advice, and requested that Sandip refrain from giving it, adding that it was futile. He then stated that he needed to inform Sandip that his followers had been secretly oppressing his tenantry, and demanded that he leave his territory.

opening.speaker: Sandip
opening.text: Sandip questioned Nikhil, asking whether the threat was due to fear of the Mussulmans or some other apprehension.
